Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment A classic late-summer Great Basin thermal day with strong, sharp lift and high ceilings. Moderate SW–W winds develop by midday, favouring west-facing launches while cross-winds will challenge east and south facing sites. Dry, no precipitation; some overdevelopment risk at Hallelujah.

Site Breakdown

  • Kingsbury Grade: Marginal – strong thermals (peak 516 fpm, ceiling 6295 ft AGL) but wind direction off preferred SE launch; cross-wind from SW–W all day. Window 12pm–2pm for thermal soaring only. Sharp thermals (lapse rate 9.8 °C/km) – advanced pilots only.
  • Hallelujah: Favorable – wind veers into preferred W–NW window from midday, strong lift (peak 585 fpm, ceiling 8338 ft AGL). Watch 23% overdevelopment risk. Window 12pm–5pm. Sharp thermals (10.1 °C/km).
  • Slide Mountain: Unfavorable – persistent SW cross-winds, very high bulk shear (27 mph), low thermal ceiling (2815 ft AGL). No reliable flying window. Sharp thermals (8.2 °C/km).
  • McClellan: Marginal – light S winds aligned 10am–11am, then wind shifts to W/NW cross. Strong potential lift (peak 607 fpm, 6020 ft AGL) but unusable after shift. Window 10am–11am for sledders. Sharp thermals (10.0 °C/km).
  • West McClellan: Favorable – wind perfectly backs into preferred W sector after 12pm, solid thermals (peak 511 fpm, ceiling 5671 ft AGL). Window 12pm–5pm. Sharp thermals (9.8 °C/km).
  • Peavine Mountain: Favorable – well-aligned SW flow, strong lift (peak 550 fpm, 5338 ft AGL), but gusty afternoon (24 mph). Window 10am–4pm. Sharp thermals (9.6 °C/km).
  • Rainbow Ridge: Marginal – wind only briefly aligns ENE at 9am, otherwise off-direction; strong thermals (615 fpm, 8183 ft AGL) but cross-wind dominates. Brief ridge/thermal window 9am. Sharp thermals (10.0 °C/km).
  • Duck Hill: Marginal – limited wind alignment (only noon WNW & late evening), strong lift (peak 556 fpm, 6445 ft AGL); hazardous 30° directional shear aloft. Brief window 12pm. Sharp thermals (9.8 °C/km).
  • Daydreams: Favorable – SW winds perfectly aligned all day, light but consistent lift (peak 221 fpm, ceiling 3508 ft AGL). Best soaring site of the day. Window 9am–6pm. Sharp thermals (8.9 °C/km).

Hazards

  • Rotor/lee turbulence: Downwind of Peavine Mountain and Carson Range ridgelines in strong SW–W afternoon flow.
  • Overdevelopment: Hallelujah 23% chance of cloud formation within thermal zone; isolated thunderstorm potential.
  • Low-level wind shear: Significant speed shear (≥5 mph/layer) at Kingsbury (5 mph at 1757 ft), Hallelujah (10 mph at 8433 ft), Slide Mountain (7 mph at 758 ft), McClellan (6 mph at 7922 ft), West McClellan (6 mph at 6244 ft), Duck Hill (6 mph at 8607 ft). Additionally directional shear of 30° at Duck Hill.

Site Forecast ?Top of Thermals (PBLH) — height of the turbulent mixing layer; thermals typically reach this ceiling.
LCL (Lifted Condensation Level) — altitude where rising air reaches its dew point; theoretical cloud base.
Cloud Base — lowest model level with >10% cloud fraction.
w* — convective velocity scale; higher = stronger thermals (ft/min).
Cloud Cover — max cloud fraction over the column (0–100%).
Wind thresholds: orange = 12 mph, red = 18 mph.
